name: Instagram
description: Run an Instagram professional (business or creator) account through Meta's Graph API: profile, posts, reels and stories, account and post insights, comments, replies and @mentions, Direct Messages, hashtag search and public business profiles. Sign in with Instagram or Facebook (no Facebook Page needed with Unified Login) or paste a token. Publishing, sending messages and deleting are installed switched off.
instructions:
## Instagram (Meta Graph API, Unified Login or Facebook Login)
This connector calls the Graph API at `https://graph.facebook.com/v25.0` for one Instagram professional account (business or creator). Personal Instagram accounts have no API access.

**Sign in (recommended).** On the connector page click **Authorize with Provider** and approve the app. Two logins, chosen by the Meta app:
- **Unified Login** (every Meta app created since autumn 2026, and AnythingMCP Cloud): sign in with the Instagram account or with Facebook, pick the business portfolio that owns the Instagram account (an account only shared into another portfolio is not granted to the app) and tick the account. No Facebook Page is needed, but the account must belong to a business portfolio (Meta creates one in the dialog if needed). AnythingMCP stores a Business Integration System User token that does not expire in `INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN` and fills in `INSTAGRAM_ACCOUNT_ID` (or asks which account when several were shared). It stops working only when the client removes the app from the business portfolio or moves the account to another portfolio: authorize again then.
- **Facebook Login** (older apps without a Unified Login configuration): sign in with a Facebook user who manages the Page linked to the Instagram account. AnythingMCP stores a long-lived user token and renews it before it expires.

On a server with its own Meta app (AnythingMCP Cloud) there is nothing else to set up. With an app of your own (self-hosted, or by choice), set `META_APP_ID` and `META_APP_SECRET` (App settings, Basic) and, for Unified Login, `META_CONFIG_ID` (Use cases, Manage messaging and content on Instagram, Customize, API setup with Unified login: the configuration id). Add `<your AnythingMCP address>/api/meta/callback` as the redirect URL of that configuration (Unified Login) or to Facebook Login's valid OAuth redirect URIs (on AnythingMCP Cloud: `https://cloud.anythingmcp.com/api/meta/callback`). An app in development mode works for people with a role on the app; serving other people needs Meta App Review (Advanced Access) and Live mode.

**Or paste a token.** Meta's Facebook Login issues no refresh tokens: a token from the login dialog or the Graph API Explorer lasts one to two hours, a long-lived user token about 60 days. The connector takes a ready token in `INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN`, in one of two ways:
1. **System User token** (never expires): Meta Business settings, Users, System users, Generate token, expiry **Never**. Grant it `instagram_basic`, `instagram_manage_insights`, `instagram_manage_comments`, `pages_show_list`, `pages_read_engagement` and `business_management`; add `instagram_content_publish` to publish and `instagram_manage_messages` for Direct Messages. Assign the Instagram account (and its Page, if any) to the system user as assets.
2. **User token, renewed automatically**: paste a user token from the Graph API Explorer (https://developers.facebook.com/tools/explorer/) with the same permissions, and set `META_APP_ID` and `META_APP_SECRET`. AnythingMCP exchanges it for a long-lived one (about 60 days) on its first call and renews it once fewer than 10 days remain. Without the app ID and secret the token is used as pasted.

A user token stops working for good when the user logs out of Facebook, changes the password or removes the app (error 190 with subcode 467, 460 or 458). The connector then answers at once with what to do instead of retrying; authorize again or paste a new token to continue.

**Which tool first.** With a Unified Login token, `instagram_list_assigned_accounts` lists the Instagram accounts the client shared (`id` and `username`); with a Facebook user or System User token, `instagram_list_linked_accounts` lists the Facebook Pages with the Instagram account linked to each (`instagram_business_account.id`). That id (a number starting with 1784) is the value for `INSTAGRAM_ACCOUNT_ID`. Then `instagram_get_account` checks the setup and returns follower and media counts. Tools that act on the account take its id from the connector, so you never pass it.

**Ids.** Media ids come from `instagram_list_media`, `instagram_list_stories` or `instagram_list_tagged_media`; comment ids from `instagram_list_comments`; hashtag ids from `instagram_search_hashtag`; the media and comment ids of an @mention from the `mentions` webhook (Meta sends them; there is no list of mentions to read). Ids are strings of digits; pass them unchanged.

**Fields.** The Graph API returns only the fields you ask for. Every read tool has a `fields` parameter with a sensible default; add fields with a comma, nested fields with braces, e.g. `children{media_url}`.

**Pagination.** List answers carry `paging.cursors.after` and `paging.next`. Call the tool again with `after` set to that cursor; when `paging.next` is missing you have the last page. `since` and `until` take Unix timestamps.

**Insights.** Account insights need `metric` and `period=day`; most metrics also need `metric_type=total_value`. Use `views` instead of `impressions` (removed in v22.0). Demographic metrics (`follower_demographics`, `engaged_audience_demographics`) need `period=lifetime`, `metric_type=total_value`, a `timeframe` and a `breakdown` (age, city, country, gender). Data can lag up to 48 hours, accounts below 100 followers return no demographics, and a metric that does not apply returns an error rather than zero. Media insights: `reach,likes,comments,saved,shares,total_interactions,views` for posts and reels, `reach,replies,navigation,views` for stories (stories expire after 24 hours).

**Hashtags.** `instagram_search_hashtag` turns a name into an id; an account can query at most 30 distinct hashtags in a rolling 7 days. Top and recent media return public posts only, without usernames. Hashtag search needs the Instagram Public Content Access feature on the app.

**Comments and mentions.** Besides reading and replying, `instagram_create_comment` posts a top-level comment on one of the account's posts, `instagram_hide_comment` hides or unhides one, `instagram_set_comments_enabled` turns commenting off or on for a post, and `instagram_delete_comment` (switched off at install) deletes one for good. `instagram_list_tagged_media` lists posts the account is tagged in; for an @mention in someone else's caption or comment, `instagram_get_mentioned_media` and `instagram_get_mentioned_comment` read it and `instagram_reply_to_mention` answers it. `instagram_list_recently_searched_hashtags` shows the hashtags already counted against the 30-a-week limit.

**Direct Messages.** `instagram_list_conversations` lists the conversations (pass `user_id` for the one with a person), `instagram_get_conversation_messages` reads one (only the 20 most recent messages carry their content), `instagram_get_message` one message and `instagram_get_user_profile` the profile of someone who wrote. `instagram_send_message` (switched off at install) answers a person within 24 hours of their last message (the standard messaging window); `instagram_send_private_reply` (switched off at install) answers a comment privately, once per comment and within 7 days. Messaging needs `instagram_manage_messages`, and the account owner must allow access to messages in the Instagram app (Settings, Messages and story replies, Message controls, Connected tools). Before sending, show the message and wait for the user's yes.

**Publishing** (switched off at install): create a container with `instagram_create_media_container`, check `instagram_get_container_status` until `status_code` is `FINISHED` (videos take a while), then `instagram_publish_media`. Media must be at a public HTTPS URL. API publishing is limited to 50 posts per 24 hours; `instagram_get_publishing_limit` shows the usage. `instagram_delete_media` (switched off at install) deletes a post, reel, story or whole carousel; it needs the `instagram_manage_contents` permission, which the sign-in does not ask for: grant it to a System User token to use it.

**Rate limits.** Business Use Case limits: about 4800 calls per 24 hours times the account's impressions. A 400 with error code 4, 17, 32 or 613 means throttled: wait and retry. Error 190 means the token expired or was revoked; error 10 or 200 means a permission is missing.

INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN.label: Access token
INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN.help: Filled in by Authorize with Provider on the connector page (recommended). To paste one instead: Meta Business settings → Users → System users → your system user → Generate token: pick your Meta app, set expiry to Never and grant instagram_basic, instagram_manage_insights, instagram_manage_comments, pages_show_list, pages_read_engagement and business_management (plus instagram_content_publish to publish). The system user must have the Facebook Page and the Instagram account assigned. A user token from the Graph API Explorer also works: set META_APP_ID and META_APP_SECRET as well and it is turned into a long-lived token and renewed automatically.

INSTAGRAM_ACCOUNT_ID.label: Instagram account ID
INSTAGRAM_ACCOUNT_ID.help: Filled in by Authorize with Provider. Otherwise the Instagram professional account id, a number starting with 1784: Meta Business settings → Accounts → Instagram accounts shows it; instagram_list_assigned_accounts (Unified Login token) or instagram_list_linked_accounts (Facebook token) returns it.
INSTAGRAM_ACCOUNT_ID.patternMessage: The account id is a number of 10 to 20 digits, usually starting with 1784. It is not the Instagram username.

META_APP_ID.label: Meta app ID (optional)
META_APP_ID.help: Leave empty on a server with its own Meta app (such as AnythingMCP Cloud). With an app of your own: developers.facebook.com → My Apps → your app → App settings → Basic → App ID. Add <your AnythingMCP address>/api/meta/callback as the redirect URL of its Unified Login configuration (or to Facebook Login's valid OAuth redirect URIs on an older app), then click Authorize with Provider. A pasted user token is also exchanged for a long-lived one and renewed with this app. Leave empty with a System User token.
META_APP_ID.patternMessage: The app ID is a number, shown under App settings → Basic.

META_APP_SECRET.label: Meta app secret (optional)
META_APP_SECRET.help: Only with an app of your own, together with META_APP_ID: App settings → Basic → App secret → Show. It is stored encrypted and sent only to graph.facebook.com.
META_APP_SECRET.patternMessage: The app secret is 32 characters, digits and the letters a to f.

META_CONFIG_ID.label: Unified Login configuration ID (optional)
META_CONFIG_ID.help: Only with an app of your own that uses Unified Login (every Meta app created since autumn 2026): Use cases → Manage messaging and content on Instagram → Customize → API setup with Unified login → the configuration id. With it, Authorize with Provider signs in with Instagram or Facebook and no Facebook Page is needed. Leave empty on AnythingMCP Cloud and for an older app that uses Facebook Login.
META_CONFIG_ID.patternMessage: The configuration id is a number, shown next to the configuration in API setup with Unified login.

prerequisites: An Instagram **business or creator** account. On AnythingMCP Cloud you just sign in with Instagram or Facebook (Unified Login, no Facebook Page needed). Elsewhere you also need a Meta app with the Instagram use case (or a **System User** token from Meta Business settings). Personal Instagram accounts have no API access.

verifyHints.400: Meta refused the request. Error 190 means the token is invalid or expired: generate a System User token with expiry Never. If the message says the object does not exist, use the 1784... account id (not the username or the Page id) and assign the Instagram account to the system user.
verifyHints.401: Meta refused the token, or it has expired (error 190). Click Authorize with Provider on the connector page, generate a System User token with expiry Never, or paste a new user token and set META_APP_ID and META_APP_SECRET so it is renewed automatically.
verifyHints.403: The token lacks a permission (error 10 or 200). Authorize again and approve every permission, or generate the token again with instagram_basic, instagram_manage_insights and instagram_manage_comments (plus pages_show_list and pages_read_engagement for a Facebook token).
verifyHints.rate_limited: Meta is throttling this account or app (error 4, 17, 32 or 613). Wait a few minutes and try again.

connector.name: Instagram API (Unified Login or Facebook Login)

tools.name: instagram_list_linked_accounts
tools.description: List the Facebook Pages a Facebook user or System User token can access, each with the Instagram professional account linked to it (instagram_business_account with id and username). Use it once during setup to find the Instagram account id. A Unified Login token has no Pages: use instagram_list_assigned_accounts.

limit.description: Pages per page of results (default 25, max 100).

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer, to read the next page.

tools.name: instagram_list_assigned_accounts
tools.description: List the Instagram professional accounts a Unified Login token can act for (the accounts the client shared when signing in), with id and username. Use it once after signing in to find or check INSTAGRAM_ACCOUNT_ID. With a Facebook user token use instagram_list_linked_accounts instead.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer, to read the next page.

tools.name: instagram_get_account
tools.description: Get the configured Instagram account's profile: username, name, biography, website, followers_count, follows_count, media_count and profile picture URL. Start here to confirm the setup works and to get the headline numbers of the account.

tools.name: instagram_list_media
tools.description: List the account's posts and reels, newest first, with caption, media_type (IMAGE, VIDEO, CAROUSEL_ALBUM), media_product_type (FEED, REELS), permalink, timestamp, like_count and comments_count. Stories are not included; use instagram_list_stories. Page with `after`; filter by date with since/until.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer.

before.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.before, to go back one page.

since.description: Only media published at or after this Unix timestamp (seconds).

until.description: Only media published before this Unix timestamp (seconds).

tools.name: instagram_get_media
tools.description: Get one post, reel or story by media id: caption, type, permalink, timestamp, like and comment counts, media URL and, for carousels, the child items. Use it after a list tool when you need the details or the current counts of a single item.

media_id.description: Media id from instagram_list_media, instagram_list_stories or instagram_list_tagged_media.

tools.name: instagram_list_stories
tools.description: List the account's stories that are live now (stories disappear from the API 24 hours after posting). Returns id, media_type, media_url, permalink and timestamp. Read story insights with instagram_get_media_insights before they expire.

tools.name: instagram_list_tagged_media
tools.description: List public posts by other accounts in which the configured account has been tagged, with caption, permalink, username of the author and timestamp. Use it to monitor user-generated content and mentions by photo tag.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer.

tools.name: instagram_get_account_insights
tools.description: Get account-level insights for the configured account: reach, views, accounts_engaged, total_interactions, likes, comments, shares, saves, follows_and_unfollows, profile_links_taps, or follower and engaged-audience demographics. Returns one entry per metric with values per day (time_series) or a total for the range (total_value).

metric.description: Comma-separated metrics, e.g. reach,views,accounts_engaged,total_interactions. Demographics: follower_demographics or engaged_audience_demographics (one per call).

period.description: day for interaction metrics, lifetime for demographic metrics.

metric_type.description: total_value returns one total for the range (needed for most metrics and all breakdowns); time_series returns daily values (reach only).

breakdown.description: Optional split: media_product_type, follow_type or contact_button_type for interactions; age, city, country or gender for demographics.

since.description: Start of the range as a Unix timestamp. The range may cover at most 30 days.

until.description: End of the range as a Unix timestamp.

timeframe.description: Required for demographic metrics instead of since/until.

tools.name: instagram_get_media_insights
tools.description: Get lifetime insights for one post, reel or story: reach, views, likes, comments, saved, shares, total_interactions, or for stories replies and navigation. Returns one entry per metric. Use it to compare how individual posts performed.

media_id.description: Media id from instagram_list_media or instagram_list_stories.

metric.description: Comma-separated metrics. Posts and reels: reach,views,likes,comments,saved,shares,total_interactions. Stories: reach,views,replies,navigation,shares.

breakdown.description: Optional split, e.g. action_type for the navigation metric of a story.

tools.name: instagram_list_comments
tools.description: List the top-level comments on one post or reel, newest first, with text, username, timestamp, like_count, hidden flag and the replies under each comment. Use it to read the conversation on a post or to find a comment id before replying.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer.

tools.name: instagram_list_comment_replies
tools.description: List the replies to one comment, with text, username, timestamp and like_count. Use it when a comment has more replies than instagram_list_comments returned inline, or to follow a single thread.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer.

tools.name: instagram_reply_to_comment
tools.description: Post a public reply, as the configured account, under a comment on one of its own posts. Returns the id of the new reply. Needs the instagram_manage_comments permission. The reply is visible to everyone at once.

comment_id.description: Id of the comment to answer, from instagram_list_comments.

message.description: Text of the reply. Up to 2200 characters; @mentions and hashtags are allowed.

tools.name: instagram_hide_comment
tools.description: Hide or unhide a comment on one of the account's own posts. A hidden comment stays visible to its author but not to anyone else. Returns success true. Needs the instagram_manage_comments permission.

comment_id.description: Id of the comment, from instagram_list_comments.

hide.description: true to hide the comment, false to show it again.

tools.name: instagram_search_hashtag
tools.description: Look up a hashtag by name and return its id, which instagram_get_hashtag_top_media and instagram_get_hashtag_recent_media need. An account may query at most 30 different hashtags in a rolling 7 days, so reuse ids within a session.

q.description: Hashtag name without the #, e.g. coffee.

tools.name: instagram_get_hashtag_top_media
tools.description: Get the most popular public posts for a hashtag, with caption, media type, permalink, like and comment counts and timestamp (no usernames). Use it to see what performs well under a hashtag; get the id from instagram_search_hashtag first.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer.

tools.name: instagram_get_hashtag_recent_media
tools.description: Get public posts tagged with a hashtag in the last 24 hours, newest first, with caption, media type, permalink, counts and timestamp. Use it to monitor a campaign or branded hashtag; get the id from instagram_search_hashtag first.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer.

tools.name: instagram_get_business_profile
tools.description: Look up another Instagram business or creator account by username (business discovery): followers_count, media_count, biography, website and its recent posts with like and comment counts. Use it for competitor or partner research. Personal accounts are not returned.

username.description: Instagram username of the other professional account, without the @.

tools.name: instagram_get_publishing_limit
tools.description: Show how many posts the account has published through the API in the current rolling 24 hours (quota_usage) and the limit (config.quota_total, normally 50). Check it before publishing several items in a row.

tools.name: instagram_create_media_container
tools.description: Step 1 of publishing: create a media container for an image, a video, a reel, a story or a carousel item from a public HTTPS URL. Returns the container id. Nothing is visible until instagram_publish_media is called with that id. Containers expire after 24 hours. Needs instagram_content_publish.

image_url.description: Public HTTPS URL of a JPEG image. Use for single images, image stories and image carousel items.

video_url.description: Public HTTPS URL of an MP4 or MOV video. Use with media_type REELS or STORIES, or for a video carousel item.

media_type.description: Leave empty for a single image post. REELS for videos, STORIES for stories, CAROUSEL for the parent of a carousel (with children), VIDEO for a video carousel item.

caption.description: Caption, up to 2200 characters, 30 hashtags and 20 @mentions. Not used for stories or carousel items.

is_carousel_item.description: true when this container is one item of a carousel that will be created afterwards.

children.description: For media_type CAROUSEL: comma-separated container ids of 2 to 10 carousel items.

cover_url.description: Reels only: public URL of a cover image.

share_to_feed.description: Reels only: also show the reel in the main feed (default true).

alt_text.description: Image posts only: alternative text for screen readers, up to 1000 characters.

location_id.description: Optional Facebook Page id of a place to tag as location.

tools.name: instagram_get_container_status
tools.description: Check whether a media container is ready to publish. status_code is IN_PROGRESS while Instagram processes a video, FINISHED when ready, PUBLISHED after publishing, or ERROR / EXPIRED with a reason in status. Poll it about once a minute for videos.

tools.name: instagram_publish_media
tools.description: Step 2 of publishing: publish a container (status FINISHED) to the account, making the post, reel, story or carousel public at once. Returns the new media id. Counts against the limit of 50 API posts per 24 hours. Cannot be undone through the API.

creation_id.description: Container id from instagram_create_media_container (for a carousel, the id of the CAROUSEL parent container).

tools.name: instagram_get_mentioned_media
tools.description: Read a post by another account whose caption @mentions this account: caption, type, media URL, link, author and counts. The media id comes from the mentions webhook (Instagram sends it when the account is mentioned).

media_id.description: Id of the post that mentions the account, from the mentions webhook.

tools.name: instagram_get_mentioned_comment
tools.description: Read a comment by another account that @mentions this account: text, time, likes and the post it was written on. The comment id comes from the mentions webhook.

comment_id.description: Id of the comment that mentions the account, from the mentions webhook.

tools.name: instagram_reply_to_mention
tools.description: Answer an @mention of this account in another account's caption or comment. With media_id alone the answer is a comment on that post; with media_id and comment_id it is a reply under the mentioning comment. Returns the new comment id.

media_id.description: Id of the post where the account was mentioned.

comment_id.description: Id of the mentioning comment. Leave empty when the mention is in the caption.

tools.name: instagram_create_comment
tools.description: Post a new top-level comment, as this account, on one of the account's own posts or reels. Returns the new comment id. To answer a comment, use instagram_reply_to_comment instead.

tools.name: instagram_set_comments_enabled
tools.description: Turn commenting on or off for one of the account's posts or reels. Existing comments stay; while it is off nobody can add new ones. Returns success true.

enabled.description: true to allow comments, false to turn them off.

tools.name: instagram_delete_comment
tools.description: Delete a comment on one of the account's posts, for everyone. This cannot be undone; instagram_hide_comment is the reversible alternative. Returns success true.

tools.name: instagram_delete_media
tools.description: Delete one of the account's posts, reels or stories, or a whole carousel (not a single carousel item). This cannot be undone. Needs the instagram_manage_contents permission. Returns success true and the deleted id.

media_id.description: Media id from instagram_list_media or instagram_list_stories; for a carousel, the carousel id.

tools.name: instagram_list_recently_searched_hashtags
tools.description: List the hashtags this account looked up with instagram_search_hashtag in the last 7 days. Each counts against the limit of 30 different hashtags a week; querying one of these again is free.

tools.name: instagram_list_conversations
tools.description: List the Direct Message conversations of the account, most recently active first, with the participants and the time of the last message. Pass user_id to find the conversation with one person. Conversations in the Requests folder inactive for 30 days are not listed.

user_id.description: Instagram-scoped id (IGSID) of a person, to get only the conversation with them.

after.description: Cursor from paging.cursors.after of the previous answer, for the next page.

tools.name: instagram_get_conversation_messages
tools.description: Read the messages of one Direct Message conversation, newest first, with sender, recipient, text and time. Only the 20 most recent messages have their content; older ones return only ids.

tools.name: instagram_get_message
tools.description: Get one Direct Message by id: sender, recipient, text, attachments and time. Only the 20 most recent messages of a conversation can be read.

message_id.description: Message id from instagram_get_conversation_messages or a webhook.

tools.name: instagram_get_user_profile
tools.description: Get the public profile of a person who messaged or commented, from their Instagram-scoped id (IGSID): name, username, profile picture, follower count and whether they follow the account or the account follows them. Works only for people who have messaged the account.

user_id.description: Instagram-scoped id (IGSID) from a conversation participant or a message sender.

tools.name: instagram_send_message
tools.description: Send a Direct Message, as the account, to a person who wrote to it. Allowed only within 24 hours of their last message (the standard messaging window). Text up to 1000 bytes; links are sent as text. Returns recipient_id and message_id.

recipient_id.description: Instagram-scoped id (IGSID) of the person, from a conversation participant or a message sender.

tools.name: instagram_send_private_reply
tools.description: Answer a comment on one of the account's posts with a private Direct Message to its author. One private reply per comment, within 7 days of the comment. Returns recipient_id and message_id.
